summary: The supplied positive accumulator rejects valid boundary values when the accumulated prefix equals max/base: its `>=` check rejects before the next digit can be checked against the remaining range. This fits failures across integer widths, but the negative accumulator is needed to account for signed minimum failures too.
hypotheses: The positive accumulator uses an inclusive quotient check that rejects valid values when the current prefix equals max/base.
The negative accumulator has the analogous boundary-check error, causing signed minimum values to fail.
